title: Use perf-canary signals as rollout gates (auto-pause/rollback criteria + Console UX + notifications)
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
## Summary
We should integrate the production perf-canary regression signals into Redwood’s rollout workflows so we can automatically pause/rollback risky runtime and model-serving changes before broad customer impact.

This ticket defines:
- Gate criteria (what constitutes a rollback/pause signal vs. a warning)
- How gates are evaluated during rollouts (scope, timing, anti-flap)
- Console UX / release UI needs (visibility + override + audit)
- Notification policies (who gets notified, where, and what links are included)

## Background / problem
We can detect regressions (p95 latency up, tokens/sec down) via the always-on perf canary. Today, those alerts are reactive (Slack + on-call). During runtime rollouts and model config changes, we still rely heavily on manual spot-checking.

Desired state: rollouts have an explicit “Performance Gate” stage that consumes canary signals, holds expansion when confidence is high, and prompts clear owner action.

## Goals
1) Prevent broad regressions by halting rollouts when canary shows sustained, high-confidence p95 / throughput regressions for impacted models.
2) Keep noise low (avoid auto-pauses from baseline drift, short-lived telemetry delays, or low sample sizes).
3) Make it explainable: gate UI should show what regressed, by how much vs baseline, confidence/sample size, and likely attribution hints (queueing vs runtime-only vs kernel tag changes).
4) Provide safe controls: explicit override with audit log, and clear runbook links.

## Non-goals (initial)
- Automatically rolling back kernel flags or runtime versions without human approval (we can revisit once signal quality is proven).
- Customer-traffic shadowing or any gating based on customer prompts.
- Quality-eval gating (owned by Applied ML / eval harness separately).

## User stories
- As Release Engineering / Runtime TL, when rolling runtime build runtime-X across regions, I want a rollout stage that pauses if top models regress > threshold so I don’t ship a bad build.
- As SRE on-call, I want the gate to create one deduped incident thread with the exact model(s)/region/SKU, baseline, observed values, and links to dashboards + runbook.
- As Product/Console user (internal), I want to see “why did the rollout pause?” and “what do I do next?” with the ability to override (with justification).

## Proposed gate model (MVP)
### Gate name
“Perf Canary Regression Gate”

### Gate scope
- Applies to: runtime releases and config rollouts that affect serving runtime behavior (scheduler/batching changes, kernel updates, runtime upgrades) and can be scoped to:
  - Region
  - Hardware SKU (when applicable)
  - Deployment tier (Hosted vs Dedicated; Private is out of scope for auto-gates initially)
- Evaluates a curated set of models:
  - “Top models” (highest traffic / highest business impact)
  - “High-risk models” (recent onboarding or recent kernel/scheduler optimization)

### Gate evaluation window
- Evaluate continuously during rollout stages, but only take action after:
  - minimum sample size reached per model (as defined by ENG-4874 baseline/threshold strategy)
  - sustained window (anti-flap) e.g., 10–15 minutes of consistent regression signals

### Gate actions
- WARNING (non-blocking):
  - Posts to #eng-runtime (and attaches to rollout page) when regression exceeds warning thresholds but doesn’t meet paging/pause criteria.
- AUTO-PAUSE (blocking):
  - Pauses rollout expansion for the affected region/tier when regression exceeds paging/pause thresholds for any “top model” OR exceeds a higher threshold for >= N models.
  - Notifies on-call + release channel with a single deduped thread.
- RECOMMEND-ROLLBACK (blocking, but human-confirm):
  - If regression sustained beyond an extended window (e.g., 30–45 minutes) or exceeds a severe threshold (e.g., very large p95 increase), gate escalates from pause to “rollback recommended” state and requires explicit ack.

### Default MVP thresholds (to be finalized with SRE + Runtime)
Gate should use the same underlying alert signals as observability-pack paging rules (ENG-4878) to reduce divergence.

Proposed mapping (illustrative; final values owned by SRE policy doc):
- p95 e2e latency: +10% (warn), +20% (pause/page)
- tokens/sec: -8% (warn), -15% (pause/page)
- require runtime-only corroboration OR queueing-time attribution before recommending rollback, to avoid pausing on pure fleet contention events (still pause-worthy, but different owner/escalation).

## Console / UX requirements (internal)
### Rollout UI
Add a “Gates” section to rollout runs:
- Gate status: Passing / Warning / Paused / Override active
- Summary: impacted models + metric deltas vs baseline
- Confidence: sample size, evaluation window, last updated
- Attribution hints: queueing vs runtime-only, kernel tag changes, runtime build id, model version
- Links: Grafana dashboard, trace explorer query, runbook (runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert)

### Override flow
- “Override and continue rollout” requires:
  - justification text
  - duration (e.g., override valid for 60 minutes)
  - approver role: runtime TL or on-call (policy decision below)
- All overrides must be audit logged and visible in the rollout timeline.

### Notifications
- When paused:
  - Post to #eng-releases and #eng-oncall with dedupe key: (release_id, region, tier, model)
  - Mention owners: runtime on-call + release captain
  - Include direct links to: dashboards + runbook + diff (runtime build/kernels) + last known good baseline id
- When warning:
  - Post to #eng-runtime only (no page), still attach to rollout details.

## Ownership / policy decisions needed
1) Who is allowed to override the gate? (proposal: runtime on-call primary; release captain secondary)
2) Do we pause on queueing-only regressions? (proposal: yes pause, but route to Infra/Fleet + SRE; do not auto-recommend rollback unless runtime-only corroborates)
3) What is the “top model list” source of truth? (proposal: control-plane config surface added in PR-19203; curated by Runtime + PM)

## Metrics + integration points
- Use perf-canary alert payload format from perf-canary PR-19244 for gate ingestion.
- Gate evaluation should read from the same aggregated metrics source as Grafana alerting (to avoid dual computations).
- Need a stable identity tuple for baseline lookup: (model_id, model_version, runtime_version/build_id, kernel_tag?, sku, region).

## Acceptance criteria
- A rollout run can enter a Paused state solely due to canary gate (without human intervention) when regression meets paging/pause thresholds.
- Paused state includes clear reason + links + impacted models/metrics.
- Override is available, audited, and time-bounded.
- Notifications are deduped and include the required context.
- SRE signs off on paging/pausing hygiene (no noisy pauses during normal variance; validated during phase-1 rollout in us-east).

## Rollout plan (product)
Phase 1 (us-east, 2–3 models):
- Gate runs in “observe-only” mode for 1 week (no pause), validate signal quality and false-positive rate.
- Enable auto-pause for top model regressions only once thresholds calibrated.

Phase 2 (expand):
- Add more models + regions; add “recommend rollback” escalation state.

## Links
- Umbrella eng: ENG-4872 Perf canary prod MVP
- Alerting policy + routing: ENG-4878
- Phase-1 rollout: ENG-4880
- Design doc: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/perf-regression-canary-design
- SRE policy doc: confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/per-model-latency-slos-and-alerting-policy

## Open questions
- How to handle telemetry pipeline lag: should gate require freshness checks (e.g., last datapoint < 2–3 min)?
- Should we gate rollouts per-model (pause only that model’s rollout) vs per-region runtime rollout (pause the whole region)? (proposal for MVP: pause the rollout stage for the whole region/tier to avoid partial unknown states)
- How to represent multi-metric regressions (latency + tokens/sec) in a single gate decision? (proposal: pause if either crosses pause threshold; include both in UI)
comments: 2026-01-10 (Paula Mendes): Created based on alignment thread with Marissa + Connor on what ‘auto-pause’ should mean. Key requirement: make pause explainable and override auditable.

2026-01-14 (Connor O’Brien): From release-eng perspective, we need an API-level gate result we can hook into rollout controller. Prefer we consume the same signal as paging alerts (ENG-4878) rather than invent a new evaluator in the rollout service.
2026-01-16 (Sean Gallagher): Strong +1 on time-bounded overrides + audit. Also want to ensure we don’t pause on pure ingestion delays—please add a freshness requirement before pausing.

2026-01-21 (Allison Grant): For UX, please include direct links that are region-aware (Grafana variables pre-filled). Also include runbook link in the rollout UI itself so release captain doesn’t have to find Slack threads.
2026-01-29 (Mateo Alvarez): OK with MVP: auto-pause only for ‘top models’ in phase 1. Any auto-rollback should be explicitly out of scope until we have at least 2 weeks of stable signal.

2026-02-03 (Rafael Mendes): For notifications, ensure incident-bot dedupe key includes release_id; otherwise we’ll merge unrelated pauses across concurrent rollouts. Also: route pause notifications to #eng-oncall and page only if sustained beyond X minutes (policy to be finalized).

2026-02-05 (Marissa Cole): Drafting Console UX for gates view. Need confirmation on override approvers and whether pause should block only expansion vs also stop the current stage’s canary ramp. Proposed: block expansion; do not automatically revert without human action.
